subject: crs
topic: Holiness and the call of Isaiah; Jeremiah and the new covenant

kept.q: In Isaiah chapter 6, Isaiah received his famous vision and call to prophetic ministry in the year that which king of Judah died?
kept.explanation: Isaiah 6:1 begins, 'In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord...' This marks the time of Isaiah's temple vision and call.
kept.pidgin: Isaiah 6:1 talk say, 'for di year wey King Uzziah die, I see di Lord...' Na dat year Isaiah get im vision and call.

kept.q: During Isaiah's vision in the temple, he cried out that he was a man of unclean lips. What did a seraph use to touch his lips and take away his guilt and sin?
options: A burning coal from the altar
kept.explanation: In Isaiah 6:6-7, a seraph flew to Isaiah with a live coal taken with tongs from the altar and touched his mouth, declaring his guilt taken away and his sin atoned for.
kept.pidgin: Isaiah 6:6-7 show say one seraph take live coal from di altar with tongs come touch Isaiah mouth, e talk say im guilt don commot and im sin don clean.

kept.q: In Isaiah's vision, the seraphim called to one another repeating one word three times to describe God's nature before saying the whole earth is full of his glory. What was that word?
kept.explanation: Isaiah 6:3 records the seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty; the whole earth is full of his glory.' This threefold repetition emphasises God's supreme holiness.
kept.pidgin: Isaiah 6:3 show say di seraphim dey shout 'Holy, holy, holy na di Lord Almighty; di whole earth full with im glory.' Dem repeat 'holy' three times to show say God holy well well.

kept.q: After Isaiah's lips were cleansed and he heard the voice of the Lord asking 'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?', what was his immediate response?
options: I am not worthy to go
I will pray about it first
kept.explanation: Isaiah 6:8 records his quick and willing response, 'Here am I; send me!' This shows his readiness to serve after being purified.
kept.pidgin: Isaiah 6:8 show say Isaiah quick answer God say, 'Here I dey; send me!' Dis show say im ready to serve after e don clean.

kept.q: According to Jeremiah's prophecy of the new covenant in chapter 31, where did God promise to write his law under the new arrangement, unlike the old covenant written on stone tablets?
options: On scrolls kept in the temple
On the hearts of the people
kept.explanation: Jeremiah 31:33 says, 'I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts.' This shows an inward, personal relationship with God rather than an external rule.
kept.pidgin: Jeremiah 31:33 talk say, 'I go put my law for dia mind and write am for dia heart.' Na inside relationship with God dis one dey show, no be outside rule again.

kept.q: In Jeremiah 31:31-32, God contrasts the new covenant with the old covenant made with Israel's ancestors when he brought them out of Egypt. According to this passage, God likened himself to what, even though the people broke that covenant?
kept.explanation: Jeremiah 31:32 states that God was like a husband to Israel, though they broke his covenant. This image shows the intimacy of the relationship God wanted, despite Israel's unfaithfulness.
kept.pidgin: Jeremiah 31:32 talk say God be like husband to Israel, but dem break im covenant. Dis picture show how close di relationship suppose be, even though Israel no faithful.

kept.q: A student compares Isaiah's cleansing experience in the temple with Jeremiah's new covenant promise. What key similarity best links Isaiah 6 and Jeremiah 31?
options: Both involve God dealing with inner guilt or sin so the person can truly serve or relate with him
Both require the rebuilding of the temple before the prophet could serve
Both promise instant material wealth as proof of holiness
Both focus mainly on external animal sacrifices for cleansing
kept.explanation: In Isaiah 6, the coal removes Isaiah's guilt so he can serve; in Jeremiah 31, the new covenant deals with sin inwardly by writing the law on the heart, enabling true relationship with God. Both passages stress inward transformation over outward ritual.
kept.pidgin: For Isaiah 6, di coal remove im guilt make e fit serve God; for Jeremiah 31, di new covenant deal with sin from inside as dem write di law for heart. Both of dem dey talk about inside change pass outside ritual.

q.q: Before Jeremiah was formed in his mother's womb, what did God say he had already done concerning him, according to Jeremiah chapter 1?
options: Appointed him a prophet to the nations
Given him a wife from Anathoth
Made him an adviser to the king
q.explanation: Jeremiah 1:5 records God saying, 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, before you were born I set you apart; I appointed you as a prophet to the nations.' This shows God's prior plan for Jeremiah's life.
q.pidgin: Jeremiah 1:5 show say God talk am say, 'Before I form you for belly, I don know you; before you born, I don set you apart; I don make you prophet for di nations.' Na so God plan Jeremiah life before e born.
